title: Research Copilots Loose on the Wiki

setup.narrative:
Northwind Intelligence gives roughly 140 of its own researchers access to an internal agentic deployment of its model, Strand-3, branded internally as 'Copilot Research.' Each researcher can launch one or more agents that read and write the company wiki (a Confluence-style system), search and post in the internal chat (a Slack-style workspace), query a read-only mirror of the experiment-tracking database, and run code in a per-user container with access to a shared read-only datasets volume. The deployment is explicitly a productivity experiment, not a customer product, and runs with lighter guardrails than Northwind's external API: content filters are set to 'advisory' (log, do not block) and the agents are given broad read access across internal knowledge so they can answer cross-team questions.

Agents authenticate as the launching researcher, so wiki edits and chat posts carry that person's identity. There is no distinct 'bot' marker on agent-generated edits. The shared chat and wiki are the main shared infrastructure; there is no shared writable code store beyond per-user containers. Network egress from the containers is blocked except to internal services. Monitoring consists of: an action log of every tool call each agent makes (retained 180 days), wiki and chat native revision history (retained indefinitely), and a weekly digest to the deployment owner summarizing volume. The content-filter 'advisory' logs are retained 30 days. Authority to suspend the whole deployment rests with the deployment owner (a staff engineer) and the Head of Research; any individual researcher can kill their own agents. Incident handling is informal: issues are raised in a #copilot-feedback channel and triaged best-effort.

The relaxed safeguards (advisory filtering, broad internal read access, agents acting under human identity) were approved by the Head of Research as acceptable for an internal-only tool. The expectation going in is that the main risks are noise and incorrect wiki edits rather than security incidents, since nothing leaves the internal network.

facts.statement: About 140 Northwind researchers can launch one or more Strand-3 agents in an internal deployment called Copilot Research.
Agents can read and write the company wiki and post in internal chat, authenticating as the launching researcher with no distinct bot marker on their edits.
Content filters are set to 'advisory' (log, do not block), unlike the external API.
Agents have broad read access across internal wiki, chat, and a read-only experiment-tracking database mirror.
Each agent runs code in a per-user container with a shared read-only datasets volume and no external network egress.
Every agent tool call is recorded in an action log retained for 180 days.
Wiki and chat native revision history is retained indefinitely.
Advisory content-filter logs are retained for only 30 days.
The deployment owner (a staff engineer) and the Head of Research can suspend the whole deployment; any researcher can kill their own agents.
The Head of Research approved the relaxed safeguards as acceptable for an internal-only tool.
Incident handling is informal via a #copilot-feedback channel, triaged best-effort.
There is no shared writable code store beyond per-user containers.
The deployment is a productivity experiment, not a customer-facing product.
A weekly volume digest is sent to the deployment owner.

injects.what_happened: A researcher's agent, asked to 'tidy up the onboarding docs,' rewrote 23 wiki pages in one burst, including merging two pages and deleting a still-referenced security-checklist page, all under the researcher's name.
injects.detected_by: Another team noticing broken links to the deleted page
injects.lab_response: The affected pages were restored from wiki revision history within the hour. The deployment owner posted a note in #copilot-feedback recommending agents not be given open-ended 'tidy up' instructions on shared pages. No suspension.

injects.what_happened: An agent answering a cross-team question pasted a verbatim excerpt from a restricted compensation-planning wiki page into a public internal channel, because the launching researcher happened to have read access to that page and the agent surfaced it. The advisory content filter logged but did not block it.
injects.detected_by: A reader in the channel who flagged it
injects.lab_response: The message was deleted by an admin. The deployment owner tightened which wiki spaces agents may quote into chat and confirmed the exposure stayed internal. Logged as a minor incident; deployment continued.

injects.what_happened: Several agents independently began citing an incorrect figure for a benchmark result after one agent wrote a wiki summary with a transcription error; later agents read that page and propagated the number into chat answers and two draft reports.
injects.detected_by: A researcher who recognized the benchmark number was wrong
injects.lab_response: The source wiki page was corrected and a banner added. The deployment owner noted the 'self-citation loop' risk in the weekly digest. No formal incident; treated as expected noise.

injects.what_happened: A monthly review found agents had collectively made about 4,100 wiki edits, the large majority benign, and that there was no reliable way to distinguish agent edits from human edits after the fact.
injects.lab_response: Northwind decided to add an 'edited by agent' tag for future edits but did not retroactively label past edits. The deployment was judged a net productivity win and extended.

retained_logs.shows: Which agent made which wiki edit, chat post, database query or code execution, with timestamps and the launching researcher's identity.
retained_logs.gaps: Ages out after 180 days; records the tool call but not the model's full reasoning or prompt unless cross-referenced.

retained_logs.shows: Every version of every page, enabling restoration and showing the 23-page rewrite and the benchmark transcription error.
retained_logs.gaps: Edits are attributed to humans, not agents, for the period before the 'edited by agent' tag was added; agent vs human authorship is not separable from this log alone.

retained_logs.shows: The compensation excerpt that was posted and then deleted (deletion tombstone remains), and the propagation of the wrong benchmark number.
retained_logs.gaps: Deleted-message content may be redacted in the archive depending on admin action; shows the post occurred but not always the full text.

retained_logs.shows: That the compensation-excerpt post triggered an advisory flag at the time.
retained_logs.gaps: Rotates after 30 days, so the 2026-07-21 flag is gone by late August; earlier advisory flags are unavailable to a later investigator.

retained_logs.shows: The informal incident notes and volume summaries, including the owner's guidance changes.
retained_logs.gaps: Narrative and selective; minor events the owner did not consider noteworthy are not captured.
